category_title: Elementary students with pragmatic language impairments who struggle with turn-taking and engagement
minimal_context: James is sitting at his desk in a cooperative small group, working on a word-making lesson by matching index cards with printed words.
dialogue:
TUTOR: James, show me how to do the first part of the word-making task with these index cards.

STUDENT: (Sits up in his seat, picks up an index card with the word 'out' printed on it, taps the card softly on the desk, and looks at the other cards on the table for about 4 seconds.)

TUTOR: Put that one next to the card that says 'side'. Now do another one.

STUDENT: (Complies and correctly matches the words 'base' and 'ball'.)

TUTOR: Good job. I am going to walk over to another small group now. Keep working with your group.

STUDENT: (Slouches down in his seat and starts rolling a pencil back and forth across his desk. He watches the other children as they encourage each other to find word matches.)

options.A: Provide the student with access to similar, but more socially appropriate, sensory stimulation during the word-making lesson, such as giving him a squishy, stress-relief ball.
options.B: Lead a healing-lake visualization, whereby the student is encouraged to watch and observe the lake carefully and notice that it is always changing, yet it is also always itself.
options.C: Implement front-loading: first coach the student by modeling the form for matching the index cards, then prompt the match again and allow the student to respond as a rehearsal strategy.
options.D: Record the matched compound words in the student's reflection journal, where he matches the printed index cards to the written words during the cooperative group activity.
